# tiny-mcp-contract

> Zero-dependency MCP tool-contract snapshots and diffs. Catch silent breaking changes between server releases.

Zero runtime dependencies. Requires Python 3.8+.

## The problem

MCP servers change their tool contracts between releases without
announcing it. A required parameter is added, a tool disappears, a type
changes, an outputSchema is dropped. Your client keeps sending the old
shape and fails at runtime.

modelcontextprotocol/servers#5414 measured 140 silent contract changes
across 66 version pairs of the reference servers, none in the changelogs.

## Install

    pip install git+https://github.com/hussain-alsaibai/tiny-mcp-contract.git

Not on PyPI yet.

## Python API

    from tiny_mcp_contract import (
        ContractSnapshot, ToolSpec, Change, ChangeKind,
        diff_snapshots, classify, is_breaking, snapshot_from_client,
    )

    old = ContractSnapshot.from_json(open("v1.json").read())
    new = ContractSnapshot.from_json(open("v2.json").read())

    for c in diff_snapshots(old, new):
        print(c.kind, c.subject, c.detail)

    if is_breaking(diff_snapshots(old, new)):
        raise SystemExit("contract broke")

    old.digest              # sha256 of the whole contract
    old.per_tool_digests()  # {"read_file": "a1b2...", ...}

## Change kinds

    BREAKING  an existing caller would now fail      breaks: yes
    GONE      a tool was removed                     breaks: yes
    NEW       a tool or optional parameter added     breaks: no
    RELAXED   the server now accepts strictly more   breaks: no
    NOTATION  cosmetic: wording, descriptions        breaks: no

The names match the taxonomy in the MCP contract-drift issue, so a diff
produced here can be compared against theirs directly.

## CLI

    tiny-mcp-contract digest contract.json        print the contract digest
    tiny-mcp-contract diff old.json new.json      diff two snapshots
    tiny-mcp-contract check base.json curr.json   exit 1 on a breaking change
    tiny-mcp-contract gate base.json curr.json    CI gate, exit 1 on breaking
    tiny-mcp-contract gate --strict base.json curr.json   fail on ANY change

Add --json to any command for machine-readable output.

## The CI gate

    tiny-mcp-contract gate contract/baseline.json contract/current.json

Exits 1 when a breaking change is present, 0 when there is none. A gate
that always returns zero is worse than no gate, because it teaches people
to ignore it.

## Guarantees

- Digests are over canonical JSON, so a server that reformats its output
  does not look like a contract change.
- The output schema is hashed separately from the input schema: a server
  that starts declaring one has changed what it promises to return.
- A version bump alone produces no changes.
- Classification is conservative: anything that could break a caller is
  reported as breaking.

## Tests

54 tests, including one that models the real server-filesystem 0.2.0 to
1.0.0 change from issue #5414. Passes on Python 3.8 through 3.12.
